name: Gujarati Kadhi
steps: Whisk the curd and gram flour together until smooth. Add the water gradually while whisking, checking the bowl’s edges for flour lumps; strain the mixture if lumps remain.
Pour into a heavy saucepan and heat over medium-low heat. Stir steadily, reaching the base and corners, until the mixture begins to simmer gently.
Add jaggery and salt and stir until dissolved. Simmer over low heat for 12–15 minutes, stirring often, until the raw gram-flour taste has cooked out and the kadhi lightly coats a spoon.
For the tempering, dry the washed curry leaves well. Heat ghee in a small pan, add mustard seeds and let them begin to pop, then add cumin and curry leaves carefully, keeping clear of splashes.
When the spices smell fragrant, pour the tempering into the simmering kadhi. Stir, simmer briefly and turn off the heat; avoid a fierce rolling boil.
Taste and adjust seasoning lightly. If the kadhi has thickened too much, stir in a little hot water and warm gently before serving with your chosen meal.
tips: Whisk well before heating and stir frequently to prevent splitting.
substitutions: Any substitution changes the recipe: recheck allergies, Jain rules and quantities.
